name: Library Stacks
desc: A camera trucking sideways along a wall of library stacks — each aisle swings open as you pass it, throwing a deep one-point vista of shelved spines converging on a lit window at its dead end, then a stack end swallows it again and the next one opens.

energy.doc: lamp output, window glow and camera drift

scale.doc: stack height vs frame (2.2 = shelving that runs off the top of the frame; the stack pitch and eye height stay fixed so this is never a no-op)

density.doc: how many stacks pack across the frame — thinner stacks, more aisles reading at once

speed.doc: rate the camera trucks past the aisles

hue.doc: timber/lamp hue; book spines scatter around it

run.doc: how deep the stacks run — 1 is a vista you cannot see the end of

style.doc: aesthetic: warm timber reading room / cold fluorescent steel vault / cyan schematic linework / hatched paper plate / form from light alone

seed.doc: spine widths, heights, colours, gilt titles and shelf labels (absolute-stack keyed, so the rhythm never repeats)
